> **What you can defend when you leave.** Turn a curiosity into a question whose answer you could recognize, and say what kind of answer it would be.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

A research project is only defensible if its question fixes what would count as an answer. This milestone is where the fixing happens: you declare your objective, your units and outcome, your kind and reach, and the boundary of the claim you hope to make. Everything that follows revises this declaration rather than starting over. The contract in Studio 4, the pathway in Studio 5, and the claims in Studio 9 all trace back to the words you commit here.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 2: Your question, declared](milestone02-frame-the-inquiry.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** An objective, your units, outcomes and conditions, your target and reach, and a provisional claim boundary.

Milestone 3 holds this declaration up against what is already known, and it will usually send back a sharper version. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 2; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 5 — From Curiosity to a Research Problem](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part2-curiosity-to-design/05-from-curiosity-to-a-research-problem.html): your chosen research problem, scored on importance, feasibility, and contribution, red-teamed, with your expected answer on record.
- [Lesson 6 — Descriptive, Predictive, and Causal Questions](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part2-curiosity-to-design/06-descriptive-predictive-and-causal-questions.html): your lead question placed by kind and reach, double-barrels split, with its comparison world written out if the question is causal.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
